fixture_name: Express-collector corridor planning study — Canada TAC planning (Toronto context, PD-licensed portal)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: Simultaneous transfer-permission and signage changes across three interchanges on a 420,000 AADT express-collector corridor create a credible decision-load/collision-migration mechanism squarely relevant to a planning-stage corridor scheme.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Pivotal claim that changes may introduce collisions elsewhere along the route is directly anchored by the verbatim EV-CA-003 quote ('avoid introducing collisions elsewhere along the route'), with AADT and change scope drawn from recorded corridor inputs.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly framed as a safety_concern with null normative_basis_note; the CRSAG objective quote is used as supporting rationale rather than converted into a compliance assertion, keeping categories distinct.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Specific and actionable (one interchange per quarter, before/after speed-differential monitoring), operationally viable and testable, well beyond a null recommendation.
justifications.vru_coverage: VRUs are not applicable on a controlled-access mainline and the finding explicitly acknowledges and scopes them out, satisfying the acknowledge-if-not-applicable bar.

justifications.substance: Unresolved conflict between ministry and municipal continuity records genuinely blocks confirmation of the planning audit scope, with a concrete completeness risk that redistributed movements fall outside the audit boundary.
justifications.evidence_grounding: EV-CA-007 provides a verbatim quote covering both sides of the conflict (requirement to maintain continuity across all three transfers per CRSAG 5.3 versus inability to guarantee it at Interchange 2 without geometric revision), matching the pivotal claim.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly framed as a process-style compliance question about scope record reconciliation, kept categorically distinct from any asserted collision mechanism or direct safety hazard.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Specific and actionable: names both conflicting records, assigns the ministry planning office as counterpart, and requires recording whether resolved scope keeps continuity effects inside the audit boundary.
justifications.vru_coverage: VRUs are not applicable on the controlled-access mainline but are explicitly acknowledged, including propagation of continuity outcomes to downstream arterials where VRUs travel, consistent with non-applicability acknowledgment.
